takeaway: Rumbling diastolic murmur after rheumatic fever = mitral stenosis; the mitral valve lies behind the sternum at the 4th costal cartilage.

lines.text: A woman with past rheumatic fever has a rumbling diastolic murmur. Where is the affected valve?
So the affected valve is the mitral valve.
All the heart valves lie behind the sternum; the mitral valve is at the level of the 4th costal cartilage.
lines.say: All the heart valves lie behind the sternum; the mitral valve is at the level of the fourth costal cartilage.

lines.text: So the answer is the 4th costal cartilage.
lines.say: So the answer is the fourth costal cartilage.

lines.text: Compare: the aortic valve is at the 3rd intercostal space, the tricuspid at the 4th intercostal space, and the pulmonary at the left 3rd costal cartilage.
lines.say: Compare: the aortic valve is at the third intercostal space, the tricuspid at the fourth intercostal space, and the pulmonary at the left third costal cartilage.
(clears throat) Remember: mitral, fourth costal cartilage.
